pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Acute Intermittent Porphyria (AIP) THE SMOKING GUN: Urine darkening to a deep port-wine hue upon light exposure, coupled with severe abdominal pain out of proportion to exam and acute neuropsychiatric/motor deterioration after fasting and CYP-inducing medications. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: A partial deficiency of porphobilinogen deaminase (PBGD) results in a critical bottleneck in the heme biosynthetic pathway. Triggers such as caloric restriction, metabolic stress, or CYP-inducing drugs (like sulfonamides and haloperidol) dramatically upregulate ALAS1. This leads to the toxic systemic accumulation of neurovisceral intermediates—specifically delta-aminolevulinic acid (ALA) and porphobilinogen (PBG)—which inflict direct axonal neuropathy, severe autonomic instability, SIADH, and central encephalopathy.
